newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Stentor launches Irish fibre optic network.
newsitem.headline: Stentor launches Irish fibre optic network.

text.p: Ireland got its first fibre optic telecommunications network system on Thursday with the inauguration of a digital network by Irish firm Stentor Plc.

Stentor executive director Patrick Cruise O'Brien said the network, whose tests were completed in October, would facilitate expansion of telecom-dependent industries in Ireland and give the country's telecommunications network a major boost.

The telecom company said it was commencing its operations under contracts already signed with the AT & T Corp and MCI Communications Corp for interconnect agreements and a third company that cannot yet be named for contractual reasons.
The contracts are worth a total 15 million minutes of traffic.

Stentor's one million Irish pound network will be the country's only fully digital network comprising a fibre optic backbone and switching centres at Dublin, Shannon and London with another switching centre in New York nearing completion, the company said.
"Ireland has a considerable amount to gain from the introduction of advanced telecommunications technology," Cruise O'Brien said.
Investment into the network has been funded from 3.3 million Irish pounds raised from the floatation in April of Stentor Plc on the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) on the London Stock Exchange.
Stentor's services will be Virtual Private Networks (VPN), wholesale market and international call centres, with the VPN being the core business.
The first VPNs are expected to be installed after Christmas and under the system companies will be able to control all their local and international telecom operations as a single internal system.
Stentor, currently focusing on Ireland, said future options for expansion included that of installing new telecom infrastructure, currently monopolised by Telecom Eireann.

"Telecom Eireann are still fighting for their exclusive right to install new infrastructure but our set-up has changed the ball game and from now they have to be our friends and not dictate the rules as before. We are in a very unusual position," Cruise O'Brien said.

The company said it plans to invest an additional 1.4 million Irish pounds in continued development of its network over the next 12 months and hopes to double its current 15-man workforce over the next nine months.
